text: A health check that only confirms the database is reachable misses most of what Chapters 2 through 4 actually built. A real health check for Overlook needs to verify that the database is online, that TDE is still active, and that recent backups actually exist.

The script wraps all three checks in one function, Test-OverlookHealth, using Invoke-DbaQuery against the failover group endpoint. Each check becomes one boolean in an ordered hashtable, and an OverallHealthy flag flips to false if any single check fails.

Checking TDE again matters because Chapter 3's security posture is only real if it's still true later — a health check that never re-verifies it would miss real configuration drift. Checking backup recency ties straight back to the Beginner capstone's backup discipline and Lesson 11's RPO target.

Because this is one function with one summary flag, Lesson 19's alerting logic only needs to ask one simple question. Next lesson scripts backup automation itself — verifying backups don't just exist, but actually restore.
